_说明: 本文件为《千年一榫》内容文案英文化的「中文原文 → 英文」映射表（波2 接线消费）；键=游戏内既有中文原文（逐字一致方可命中），值=英文翻译。
结构：仅两个键——「_说明」（加载器忽略的说明数组）与「翻译」（对象）；UTF-8 无 BOM、禁注释、禁尾逗号。映射缺键时消费方回退显示中文原文。

术语表：榫卯=mortise-tenon (sunmao)；锐眼=Keen Eye；天赋值=Talent；衣橱=Wardrobe；见证者=the Witness；晷=Gui；体素=voxel；河姆渡=Hemudu；宋/元/明/现代=Song/Yuan/Ming/Modern；《营造法式》=Yingzao Fashi；斗栱=dougong；圈椅=round-backed chair；非遗=intangible cultural heritage。
格式串：含 %d/%s/%02d 等占位符的条目为格式串，占位符必须原样保留（如「天赋值：%d」→"Talent: %d"）。
UI 短词（确定/取消/返回等）本归波2，但按「宁多勿漏」原则一并收录，与 UI 侧翻译重复无害。

翻译.【河姆渡榫卯木构件】\n时间：距今约七千年的新石器时代（河姆渡文化）。\n地点：:
[Hemudu Mortise-Tenon Timber Member]
Era: Neolithic, roughly 7,000 years ago (Hemudu culture).
Location: Hemudu site, Yuyao, Zhejiang.
Type: Timber structural mortise-tenon building member.
Historical significance: One of the earliest mortise-tenon artifacts yet discovered, regarded as the source of China's timber construction.
翻译.【保国寺瓜棱柱斗拱】\n时间：北宋（11 世纪初）。\n地点：浙江宁波保国寺。\:
[Baoguo Temple Melon-Rib Column and Dougong]
Era: Northern Song (early 11th century).
Location: Baoguo Temple, Ningbo, Zhejiang.
Type: Timber dougong brackets and melon-rib column.
Historical significance: One of the oldest timber buildings surviving in Jiangnan, a testament to the maturity of Song mortise-tenon craft.
翻译.【真如寺梁架榫卯】\n时间：元代（14 世纪）。\n地点：上海真如寺。\n类型：:
[Zhenru Temple Beam-Frame Mortise-Tenon]
Era: Yuan dynasty (14th century).
Location: Zhenru Temple, Shanghai.
Type: Timber beam-frame mortise-tenon.
Historical significance: A precious surviving Yuan timber frame, bearing witness to the craft's continuity in vernacular building.
翻译.【明式黄花梨圈椅】\n时间：明代（15~17 世纪）。\n地点：江南地区。\n类:
[Ming-Style Huanghuali Round-Backed Chair]
Era: Ming dynasty (15th–17th centuries).
Location: Jiangnan region.
Type: Huanghuali (rosewood) furniture—round-backed chair.
Historical significance: A signature work of Ming-style furniture, the summit of mortise-tenon craft in everyday objects.
翻译.【参数化木构节点】\n时间：当代。\n地点：数字设计与工程实践。\n类型：参数化:
[Parametric Timber Node]
Era: Contemporary.
Location: Digital design and engineering practice.
Type: Parametrically designed timber node.
Historical significance: The mortise-tenon tradition joined with digital fabrication, exploring the contemporary form of timber architecture.
翻译.一段跨越七千年的相遇：当古老的手从画面深处伸来，与今日的手即将相触，见证之旅由此: An encounter across seven thousand years: as an ancient hand reaches out from deep within the screen, about to touch the hand of today, the journey of the Witness begins. After clearing the game, you may return here at any time to revisit this opening.
翻译.本相者，万般神通之所自出——初心是也。粗布围裙裹未凿之璞，一手执刨，一手抱梁。围: The True Form is the wellspring of every craft—the beginning heart itself. A coarse cloth apron wraps the unhewn jade; one hand holds the plane, one arm cradles the beam. The deepest old stain on the apron marks where the plane has fallen a thousand times.
翻译.玉尺者，宋人之神理也。素袍玉簪，袖中自有一部《营造法式》。以材为祖，以分为度，举: The Jade Ruler is the divine measure of the Song. Plain robe, jade hairpin—and in the sleeve, a copy of the Yingzao Fashi. Timber for ancestry, fen for measure; pitch and rise reckoned, brackets ruled, true to the finest hair. Worn, every ink line falls as if reciting the old rules.
翻译.苍梁者，大木之雄也。毡帽革带，弯刀在腰，敢以巨额承千钧。佩之，胸怀便阔：梁不怕粗: The Azure Beam is the hero of heavy timber. Felt hat, leather belt, curved blade at the waist—daring to bear a thousand-weight upon great frames. Worn, the chest grows broad: beams need not fear thickness, columns need not fear girth; great timber finds great use, without trimming the foot to fit the shoe.
翻译.缠枝者，线脚之神也。水墨衣带，当风婉转。巧不在力吼，而在圆熟：边抹起线一气贯通，: The Intertwining Vine is the spirit of moldings. An ink-wash sash, drifting graceful on the wind. Its skill is not brute force but round mastery: edge and bevel run in one unbroken line; the wrapped-leg curve shows no corner. Worn, even hardwood yields a gentle will.
翻译.衍数者，今之神机也。素衣执扇，扇中参数列列，榫卯纳于其中。古人运斤，今人运算；算: The Derived Numbers are the divine engine of today. Plain robes, a fan in hand, its face lined with parameters, mortise-tenon folded within. The ancients swung the axe; we of now compute—and at the finest precision, one must still test the fit with one's own hands. The wind beneath the fan comes from thousands of years.
翻译.抱节者，雪豹山灵也。怀中竹筒，抱之如抱柱，寒天不放手。竹有节，木有理，榫有卯——: Holding Fast is the snow-leopard mountain spirit. A bamboo tube clasped to the chest like a pillar, never loosed in the cold. Bamboo has nodes, wood has grain, the tenon has its mortise—the node is the wood's bone, the craftsman's faith. Worn, even the most tangled work keeps its measure.
翻译.运斤者，豹童也。红帔小槌，击竹有声，如磬如梆。匠石运斤成风，非力大，是心手相忘。: Master Stroke is the leopard child. Red cape, little mallet, striking bamboo in notes like chime and clapper. Master Shi swung his axe like wind—not for strength, but heart and hand forgotten in each other. Worn, the hammer lands true: where it falls is the ink line, stopping at seven parts force.
翻译.髹饰者，狸奴也。对镜理奁，奁中是漆，镜里是器。披麻捉灰凡三层，方上漆，一器髹毕千: Lacquerwork is the cat companion. Facing the mirror to arrange the case; within the case, lacquer; within the mirror, the vessel. Three layers of hemp and ash before the lacquer goes on—one vessel so finished will not rot in a thousand years. Worn, whatever passes beneath the hand takes on a sheen.
翻译.煨木者，狐女也。掌中一釜，火候在心。欲曲一木，以文火徐煨，趁热就势，曲而不折。佩: Fire-Bent is the fox maiden. A pot in her palm, the heat's timing in her heart. To bend a length of wood: simmer it slow over a gentle fire and, while warm, ease it into its curve unbroken. Worn, hasty matters can slow, and the hardest places can bend.
翻译.津梁者，九尾灵狐也。秉灯立于小桥，桥下花影，桥上灯明。桥是木作的菩萨心：肯弯腰，: Lantern Bridge is the nine-tailed spirit fox. Lantern in paw upon a little bridge: flower shadows below, lamplight above. The bridge is the Bodhisattva heart of woodwork—willing to bend, willing to bear. Worn, at every perilous pass a thread of passage opens.
翻译.斫轮者，莲上童子也。怀中一轮，徐徐而运。轮扁斫轮，得于手应于心，口不能言——真正: Wheelwright is the child upon the lotus. A wheel in his arms, turned slowly on. Wheelwright Bian carved his wheels: the hand obtains it, the heart answers it, the mouth cannot say it—the true measure is not in books, but in the hands. Worn, the slower, the truer.
翻译.牵丝者，荷荡少年也。肩荷白藕，藕丝细如墨线，韧胜胶漆。藕断丝连，丝连者榫之神也：: Drawing Silk is the youth of the lotus marshes. White lotus root across the shoulder, its threads fine as ink lines, tougher than glue and lacquer. The root breaks, the threads hold—holding is the tenon's soul: take the vessel apart, and its spirit stays whole. Worn, whatever passes through the hands keeps faith with what came before.
翻译.烹鲜者，炎童也。一手执串，一手掣火，火在肘腋而不燎眉。治木如烹鲜：文火焙之，猛火: Skewer and Flame is the fire child. A skewer in one hand, the flame in the other—fire at his elbow, yet never singeing a brow. Tending wood is like cooking a fresh catch: bake it slow, strike it fierce, all according to what the moment calls. Worn, when the timber runs dry, you know when to advance and when to yield.
翻译.执柯者，竹林豹女也。身负行囊，穿篁而过，叶声如雨。伐柯伐柯，其则不远——手中旧器: Axe in Hand is the leopard maiden of the bamboo grove. Pack on her back, threading the green, leaves raining sound. “Hewing a haft, hold a haft—the model is never far”: the old tool in hand was learned from the one before it. Worn, every stroke carries a lineage.
翻译.夯歌者，瓜田少年也。巨槌在肩，白犬相随，号子一起，落硪处尘土微颤。筑基不打诳语，: Ramming Song is the boy of the melon field. Great mallet on the shoulder, white dog at the heel; when the work chant rises, the dust trembles where the rammer falls. A foundation tells no lies—every ramming blow must be tamped true. Worn, the work underfoot is honest above all.
翻译.执矩者，顶瓜小童也。方瓜如玺，覆于头上——瓜可方，木亦可方。矩在头顶如在三尺上，: Keeper of the Square is the little gourd child. A square gourd like a seal set upon the head—what is square for the gourd is square for the wood. The square held overhead as if held three feet above; the heart upright, the line upright. Worn, no stock is wasted: level across, plumb down.
翻译.燔芝者，树栖游子也。青焰一簇，慢煨灵芝，白犬守于侧。火候急不得也熄不得，性子焙顺: Roasting Lingzhi is the wanderer of the treetops. A tuft of blue flame slow-simmering the lingzhi, a white dog keeping watch. The heat may neither hurry nor die; temper the disposition smooth, and the wood will neither warp nor crack. Worn, the long night can be kept.
翻译.磨镜者，卷发夫人也。手摇一磨，碾的是豆，磨的是性子。器面欲光，先磨其心。佩之，凡: Mirror Polisher is the curled-hair lady. Turning the grindstone by hand: beans are ground, but temper more so. For a surface to shine, first grind the heart. Worn, whatever leaves the hands can be polished to hold a reflection, without a single burr.
翻译.悬河者，执壶夫人也。银膏一倾，如瀑倒悬，分寸全在腕底：多一线则溢，少一线则虚。佩: Hanging River is the lady with the ewer. Silver paste tipped out like an upended waterfall, every fraction resting on the wrist: a hair too much overflows, a hair too little falls short. Worn, you can pour the cup brimming and still hold back the final drop.
翻译.白驹者，踏球小马也。蹄下有球，口衔一灯，灯不灭工不停。白驹过隙，千年一瞬，惟榫卯: White Colt is the ball-treading pony. A globe beneath the hooves, a lamp in the teeth: while the lamp burns, the work goes on. A white col flashes past the crack—a millennium in a blink—only mortise-tenon can hold time still. Worn, you grow familiar with the hours, and the work completes itself when it is ready.
翻译.品泉者，执盏夫人也。啜饮之间，眉目安然。识材如品泉：一眼辨其性，一叩知其声。佩之: Tasting the Spring is the lady with the cup. Between sips, brow serene. Reading timber is tasting spring water: one look discerns its nature, one knock tells its voice. Worn, not a single piece of wood is misused; every material finds its proper place.
翻译.踩岁者，骑禽小娘子也。足下灵禽，一路碎响，如踏芝麻秸——碎碎平安，岁岁有今朝。佩: Lucky Footfalls is the little dame riding a bird. A spirit fowl beneath her feet crackling along the road like sesame stalks—crack by crack, peace; year by year, this day returns. Worn, every new start carries an omen of luck, and every step lands on solid ground.
翻译.梅妆者，新岁贵人也。冠上梅开，鬓边龙影，喜气如披红。器物亦有妆：雕刻一两分，是给: Plum Adornment is the noble one of the new year. Plum blossoms on the crown, dragon shadows at the temples, joy like festival red. Vessels too may be adorned: a cut of one or two parts is dressing them in red. Worn, even the plainest timber comes into flower.
翻译.伏枥者，火鬃小马也。卧于书箱之侧，鬃尾犹带余焰。老骥伏枥，歇着不是不走了。新材静: Stabled Steed is the fire-manned pony. Lying beside the book chest, mane and tail still carrying embers. The old steed at rest in the stable is not done with roads: new timber must lie quiet for years before it becomes a great vessel. Worn, you know when to strive and when to wait.
翻译.挑灯者，双灯童子也。赤发如焰，两肩挑灯。灯下看墨线，比日头下更直——心静了，线就: Lantern Bearer is the double-lantern child. Hair red as flame, lanterns hung from both shoulders. Ink lines look straighter under lamplight than under the sun—when the heart is still, the line is straight. Worn, the long night has company, and the lamp lights of itself.
翻译.鱼龙者，跨鲤童子也。鱼灯为骑，纸扇为鞭，一夜鱼龙舞。鱼灯骨架不过十几根竹篾，游起: Fish-Dragon Lantern is the child astride the carp. A fish lantern for a mount, a paper fan for a whip—the night of dancing fish and dragons. The lantern's skeleton is barely a dozen bamboo strips, yet it swims like something alive. Worn, wherever heavy things move lightly, there is craft.
翻译.向阳者，一株花也。陶盆浅土，终日随日头转身。木性亦然：受光面紧，背光面松——识得: Sunward is a single flower. Clay pot, shallow soil, turning all day to follow the sun. The wood's nature is the same: tight on the lit side, loose on the shaded—know the sunward face, and you know the wood's temper. Worn, every cut runs with the grain.
翻译.莳花者，蓝铃园丁也。草帽素裙，盆盆罐罐皆是活计。养木如养花：锄轻水匀，移对时辰。: Planting Flowers is the bluebell gardener. Straw hat, plain dress, every pot and jar a task. Raising wood is raising flowers: hoe lightly, water evenly, move at the right hour. Worn, whatever passes through the hands slowly comes alive.
翻译.星涡者，衔烟斗的画师也。满身漩涡如星河倒卷——连天上的云都长成木纹。瘿木之涡，皆: Star Vortex is the painter with the pipe. Whorls upon whorls, like the Milky Way wound backward—even the clouds above grow into wood grain. The burl's swirls are all drafts sketched by the years. Worn, even in the roughest blank you can read the composition.
翻译.守拙者，画架上一卵也。不着一色，素到极处。大巧若拙——最高的手艺往往像没动手。佩: Keeping Simple is an egg upon an easel. Not one color laid on, plain to the extreme. Great skill looks clumsy—the highest craft often looks as if hands never moved. Worn, you will commit to the slow labor: only that one piece can be passed down ten years.
翻译.鉴形者，携镜少女也。卵者圆之极，镜者明之极。木匠以目为镜：梁直不直，吊起一望便知: Mirror of Forms is the maiden with the looking glass. The egg is roundness perfected; the mirror, brightness perfected. The carpenter makes a mirror of the eye: hang the beam, and one glance tells if it runs true. Worn, clear of heart and sharp of eye—not one hair of crookedness passes unmarked.
翻译.守藏者，绿窗贵妇也。深坐雕木之阁，掌上明珠覆以琉璃。器物传到今天，靠的不是结实，: Keeper of Heirlooms is the noblewoman at the green window. Seated deep in her carved wooden tower, the pearl in her palm covered with glaze. What brings vessels down to today is not toughness—it is someone keeping them. Worn, every old plank and weathered stock finds its place of honor.
翻译.结庐者，檐下小兽也。草亭一座，糖串一枚，躲在自家屋顶下。捆扎结顶是人类最早的房子: Raising the Hut is the little beast beneath the eaves. One grass pavilion, one candy skewer, tucked under its own roof. Lashing and binding was humanity's first house—before mortise-tenon, there was the knot. Worn, you build well from nothing at all.
翻译.绳墨者，帽肆匠人也。软尺一抖，尺寸了然。绳墨是匠人的规矩：曲直自此定，方圆自此分: Ink Line is the craftsman of the hat stall. One flick of the soft rule and the measures stand clear. The ink line is the craftsman's law: crooked and straight are settled here, square and round divided here; off by half a hair, do it over. Worn, your measure of people and of things runs true.
翻译.借景者，伞下夫人也。足下木台，一池睡莲，天光云影不请自来。造园贵在借：借远山，借: Borrowed Scenery is the lady beneath the parasol. A wooden dais underfoot, a pool of water lilies; sky-light and cloud-shadows arrive uninvited. In garden-making, all is borrowing: borrow the far hills, borrow the slanting sun. Worn, even the smallest workshop can hold heaven and earth.
翻译.叠石者，鸣镲小郎也。铜镲一击，石子三叠如小山。叠山讲一个「压」字：石互压而生稳，: Stacked Stones is the little lad of the ringing cymbals. One clash of the brass, and pebbles stack three-high like a small hill. Stacking hills turns on one word—press: stones pressing on stones stand stable; wood pressing on wood rests secure. Worn, even the most tangled situation can be set right.
翻译.穿山者，抱鳞小郎也。怀里金甲穿山兽，穿石如泥。凿卯如穿山：一寸一寸进，不响不噪，: Mountain Piercer is the little lad cradling scales. A golden-armored pangolin in his arms, going through stone as through mud. Cutting a mortise is piercing a mountain: advance an inch at a time, no din, no fuss, stop the moment you arrive. Worn, no hardwood is too hard for the chisel.
翻译.凿岩者，冠兽小匠也。帽上金兽镇着，石槌起落，顽石让路。基在岩上，屋才立得千年——: Chiseling Rock is the little mason crowned with the beast. The golden beast on the cap keeps guard; the stone mallet rises and falls, and stubborn rock makes way. Only a base upon rock lets a house stand a thousand years—the proudest frame grows out of a crack in the stone. Worn, you will gladly do the groundwork.
翻译.启函者，破罐雏鸟也。一声脆响，天光灌进罐里——壳外还有天。开榫如启函：封得住才开: Breaking the Shell is the chick split from the jar. One crisp crack, and daylight floods the pot—beyond the shell there is sky. Opening a joint is opening the case: only what seals well can be opened well; what is not broken is not revealed. Worn, at every deadlock you dare the first cut.
翻译.理匣者，拾贝海娘也。珊瑚贝壳各归各位，一箱虽小，装得下一片海。收工如收箱：工具归: Sorting the Chests is the shell-gathering daughter of the sea. Coral and shells each to their place; the chest is small, yet holds a whole sea. Closing the shop is closing the chest: tools to their stations, offcuts into their cells. Worn, hand you a snarl of hemp, and in a few strokes you'll find the thread.
翻译.圆光者，水阁鲛后也。端坐圆窗之内，水母替她挑着水晶帘。圆光罩是木作绝活：一木镂空: Halo Screen is the mer-queen of the water pavilion. Seated within the round window, jellyfish holding up her crystal curtain. The round-halo screen is a woodwork marvel: one timber pierced through, divided yet unbroken. Worn, nothing screened away or hidden slips past you.
翻译.悬鱼者，袋中金鳞也。碧水一囊，游鱼自在。古人在山墙悬一枚木鱼：水克火，木构最怕火: Hanging Fish is the golden scales in the pouch. A bag of green water, fish swimming at ease. The ancients hung a wooden fish on the gable: water conquers fire, and timber frames fear it most. Worn, you go out and in in safety; wherever you arrive, open flames keep themselves in check.
翻译.落墨者，踏浪鲛姬也。符卷随身，朱印在侧，衣袂不湿。墨线一弹，百柱归位——纸上画符: Setting the Ink is the shark-princess walking the waves. Charm scrolls about her, vermilion seal at her side, sleeves never wet. One snap of the ink line, and a hundred columns take their places—a talisman drawn on paper, a line snapped on timber. Worn, the first stroke lands true, and nothing needs doing twice.
翻译.潜渊者，着褂渊童也。立于水底卵石之上，口吐珍珠，呼吸自如。沉得下去才浮得上来：木: Diving the Depths is the deep child in his jacket. Standing on pebbles at the bottom, pearls at his lips, breathing freely. Only what sinks well can rise well: how much water the wood holds, one touch will tell. Worn, the deeper you go, the steadier you are.
翻译.负笈者，海府书生也。头顶墨玉，怀抱典籍，走一路读一路。书上得来的终究要过手——读: The Wandering Scholar is the scholar of the sea court. Ink-jade upon his head, classics in his arms, reading as he goes. What is won from books must still pass through the hands—ten thousand volumes read, and ten thousand timbers cut. Worn, any drawing, once seen, is remembered whole.
翻译.横经者，贝阙观书人也。倚珠贝之床，周身明珠低照。手艺有止境，问学无止境。佩之，肯: Reading the Classics is the reader in the shell-palace. Reclining on a bed of pearl and shell, low light of bright pearls all around. Craft has its limits; learning has none. Worn, you will return to the old ledgers: the errors and the cleverness of those before you, all remembered.
翻译.枕涛者，鲸月少年也。卧于贝床，耳边是一整片海。潮起潮落如千年松涛——木原是海的近: Pillowed on Waves is the youth of the whale-moon. Lying on his bed of shells, a whole ocean sounding in his ears. Tide rising, tide falling, like a thousand years of sighing pines—wood and sea are close kin. Worn, where the heart grows broad, the wood straightens of itself.
翻译.对上手的心境有稍许的提升: A slight boost to the mindset for settling into work
翻译.对落墨的精准度有明显的提升: A marked boost to the precision of the ink line
翻译.对承重的胆气有较大的提升: A notable boost to the nerve for bearing weight
